mainTopic: How ארץ ישראל was divided (יוצאי מצרים or באי הארץ): רב פפא's challenges from the פסוק, בנות צלפחד and בני יוסף, and אביי's rejected inference that everyone received a share.
overview: The גמרא keeps testing the view that ארץ ישראל was divided among those who entered the land (באי הארץ) rather than those who left Egypt (יוצאי מצרים). First, the פסוק 'לרב תרבו נחלתו' seems to teach something obvious under that view, and the גמרא leaves it as a קשיא. Then רב פפא asks אביי why בנות צלפחד complained, since their father never entered the land. The answer is that they were claiming their share of their grandfather חפר's land when the portions were 'returned' to the generation that left Egypt. רב פפא next asks why בני יוסף complained about too small a portion. The answer is that they had many young children who got no share. אביי then infers that nobody else was left without land, because anyone left out would have protested and the protest would be recorded. The גמרא rejects his proof: the failed protest of בני יוסף was written only to teach a lesson about guarding against עין הרע, as יהושע told them to hide in the forests.

steps.title: The verse about larger families is hard to explain if the land went to those who entered
steps.stepSummary: Under the view that ארץ ישראל was divided by באי הארץ, the פסוק 'לרב תרבו נחלתו' seems to say something obvious. The גמרא leaves this as a קשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says the land was divided among those who entered it, what does 'To the many you shall give more inheritance' teach us? This is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a question against the view of באי הארץ and admits it has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each person who entered the land gets a share, a bigger family automatically gets more land, so the פסוק adds nothing. Under the view of יוצאי מצרים, the פסוק has a real message. The single word קשיא means the question stands, but the view is not thrown out.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who entered the land of Israel
To the many you shall give more inheritance (a פסוק about dividing the land)
It is a difficulty; the question is left unanswered
But according to the one who says...

steps.confusionAlert: קשיא is not a full rejection. It means the question has no answer here, but the view of באי הארץ is still standing.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says the land was divided among those who entered the land,
what does "To the many you shall give more inheritance" teach?
It is a difficulty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לְבָאֵי הָאָרֶץ, מַאי ״לָרַב תַּרְבּוּ נַחֲלָתוֹ״? קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a בשלמא question begun just before this text.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the land was divided by באי הארץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that view the פסוק teaches something obvious, so it would be unnecessary.

steps.title: Why did בנות צלפחד complain?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי why בנות צלפחד demanded land if only people who entered the land received portions. צלפחד died in the desert and never entered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Granted, if the land went to those who left Egypt, that explains why בנות צלפחד cried out. But if the land went to those who entered the land, why did they cry out? Their father was not there to take a share!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא raises a second challenge against the view of באי הארץ, using the story of בנות צלפחד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צלפחד left Egypt but died before entering the land. If portions went to יוצאי מצרים, he had a share and his daughters could claim it. If portions went only to באי הארץ, he had no share, so his daughters seemingly had nothing to claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted; this works well according to...
He is not there to take

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Granted, according to the one who says the land was divided among those who left Egypt,
that is why the daughters of Tzelofchad were crying out.
But according to the one who says it was divided among those who entered the land,
why did they cry out?
After all, he was not there to take a share!
phrases.notes: "He" is צלפחד, who died in the desert before the land was entered.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לְיוֹצְאֵי מִצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against the same view of באי הארץ.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the land was divided by באי הארץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: צלפחד never entered the land, so under this view he had no share for his daughters to claim.

steps.title: They were claiming their grandfather's share when the land was returned
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that בנות צלפחד were claiming a share from the 'returning' of the land to the generation that left Egypt, through their grandfather חפר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they cried out about the returning of the land, and they wanted to take a share in the property of חפר.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא's question so that the view of באי הארץ still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even under the view of באי הארץ, the land was later 'returned' and counted again by the fathers and grandfathers who left Egypt. חפר, צלפחד's father, left Egypt, so a share came to him. צלפחד's daughters claimed their father's part of חפר's property.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'returning' of the portions back to the generation that left Egypt
The property of חפר, צלפחד's father

steps.whatToRemember: Even under the view of באי הארץ, the idea of חזרה means the generation that left Egypt still matters for inheritance.

phrases.english: Rather, they cried out about the returning,
phrases.notes: The land was passed back up to the generation that left Egypt and then shared out again among their heirs.

phrases.english: and they wanted to take a share in the property of Chefer.
phrases.notes: חפר was צלפחד's father, so the daughters were claiming through their grandfather.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about בנות צלפחד.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what the daughters were claiming
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The daughters were claiming their father's own direct portion, which he never had under this view.
steps.terutzMaskana: They were claiming their father's part of their grandfather חפר's share, which came back through the 'returning' (חזרה).

steps.title: Why did בני יוסף complain?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks why בני יוסף complained about a small portion if the land was divided by באי הארץ, since every one of them who entered got a share.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, if the land went to those who left Egypt, that explains why בני יוסף cried out, as it is written: 'וַיְדַבְּרוּ בְּנֵי יוֹסֵף' (And the children of יוסף spoke). But if it went to those who entered the land, why were they crying out? They all took a share!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא raises a third challenge against the view of באי הארץ, using the complaint of בני יוסף in ספר יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בני יוסף grew very large in the desert. If shares followed the smaller number who left Egypt, their portion would be too small, so their complaint makes sense. If shares followed those who entered, each of them got his own share, so there was nothing to complain about.

keyTerms.meaning: The descendants of Yosef (the tribes of מנשה and אפרים)

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says the land was divided among those who left Egypt,
that is why the children of Yosef were crying out,
as it is written: "And the children of Yosef spoke."
But according to the one who says it was divided among those who entered the land,
what were they crying out about?
They all took a share!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לְיוֹצְאֵי מִצְרַיִם, הַיְינוּ דְּקָא צָוְוחָן בְּנֵי יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי answered the second question, רב פפא brings a third challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the land was divided by באי הארץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every person who entered received his own share, a large tribe would get a large portion and would have no reason to complain.

steps.title: They complained because of their many young children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בני יוסף complained because they had many young children who did not get a portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: They complained because of the young children, since they had many of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב פפא's question from Step 4. בני יוסף complained because their large number of young children did not bring in extra land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא asked: if land went to באי הארץ, everyone who entered got a share, so what was there to complain about? The answer is that the shares were not enough for their families, because they had many young children who did not receive portions of their own.

phrases.english: Because of the young children,
since they had many of them.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under באי הארץ, everyone who entered got a share, so בני יוסף had no reason to complain.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their complaint was about their many young children, who did not add to their share.

steps.title: אביי infers that nobody was left without a share
steps.stepSummary: אביי infers that every person received land, because anyone left out would have protested and the protest would have been recorded.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Learn from this that there was not one person who did not take a share. If you thought someone did not take a share, he should have cried out.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a conclusion from the fact that the פסוקים only record the complaints of בנות צלפחד and בני יוסף. He reasons that no one else was left without land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic is simple: a person who was left out would surely have protested. Since no other protest is recorded, no one else was left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, we can conclude
If it would enter your mind, if you thought

phrases.english: אביי said: Learn from this
phrases.notes: From this he means the fact that only these two complaints are written in the פסוקים.

phrases.english: that there was not one who did not take a share;
for if you would think
that there was one who did not take,
he should have cried out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new inference from the recorded complaints discussed in Steps 2-5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone received a share of the land, since no other protest is recorded.

steps.title: אביי blocks the idea that only successful protests were recorded
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects a possible answer: maybe the פסוק only records protests that worked. The case of בני יוסף shows that a failed protest was also recorded.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: the פסוק wrote about a protest that worked and did not write about a protest that failed. But look at בני יוסף: they protested, it did not work, and the פסוק wrote about them!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers an objection someone could raise against his proof. Maybe people did protest, but the פסוקים skipped protests that failed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The possible objection is that only successful protests got recorded. אביי rejects it, because the protest of בני יוסף failed and still appears in the פסוקים. So a silent פסוק really does mean nobody protested.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible objection)

phrases.english: And if you would say:
one who cried out and it worked, the verse wrote,
phrases.notes: This is בנות צלפחד: they protested and got their land.

phrases.aramaic: דִּצְוַוח וְלָא אַהֲנִי – לָא כַּתְבֵיהּ קְרָא;
phrases.english: one who cried out and it did not work, the verse did not write;
but look at the sons of Joseph,
who cried out and it did not work,
and the verse wrote them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: דִּצְוַוח וְאַהֲנִי כַּתְבֵיהּ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends אביי's inference in Step 6 against a possible objection.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the תורה records only successful protests.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The failed protest of בני יוסף is recorded, so the suggestion does not hold.

steps.title: בני יוסף were recorded to teach good advice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects אביי's proof: the protest of בני יוסף is recorded for a special reason, to teach that a person should guard himself from עין הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the פסוק teaches us good advice: a person should guard himself from the evil eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against אביי. The case of בני יוסף is written for a different purpose, so it does not prove that failed protests are normally recorded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי relied on בני יוסף to show that failed protests are written down. The גמרא answers that this case is an exception, written to teach a lesson about עין הרע. So other failed protests could have happened and gone unrecorded, and אביי's proof falls apart.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying בני יוסף's protest worked. It agrees the protest failed, but says the פסוק recorded it only to teach a lesson.

phrases.english: There, good advice
phrases.notes: There means the case of בני יוסף. The usual rule, that failed protests are not written, still stands.

phrases.english: it teaches us,
that a person should
guard himself from the evil eye.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם עֵצָה טוֹבָה קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support אביי brought in Step 7 from בני יוסף.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's use of בני יוסף, and so his whole inference that everyone took a share.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case of בני יוסף is recorded for a special lesson, so it does not show that failed protests are normally recorded.

steps.title: יהושע told them to hide in the forests
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its reading with יהושע's reply to בני יוסף: go hide in the forests so the evil eye will not rule over you.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what יהושע told them, as it is written: 'And יהושע said to them: If you are a great people, go up to the forest.' He said to them: Go and hide yourselves in the forests, so the evil eye will not have power over you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to show that the story of בני יוסף really is about עין הרע. יהושע's answer to them is read as advice to hide from the evil eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע's words 'go up to the forest' are read as 'hide yourselves among the trees'. A large, visible people attracts עין הרע, so יהושע advised them to stay out of sight. This confirms that the lesson of the passage is about עין הרע.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is (what is meant by)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי tried to prove that everyone received land, since no other protests are recorded. The גמרא rejected his proof: בני יוסף's failed protest was recorded only to teach the lesson of guarding against עין הרע, as יהושע told them to hide in the forests.

phrases.english: And this is what Joshua said to them,
as it is written: 'And Joshua said to them,
If you are a great people,
go up to the forest.'
He said to them:
Go and hide yourselves in the forests,
so that the evil eye will not have power over you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a פסוק to support the claim in Step 8 that the episode teaches about עין הרע.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the story of בני יוסף was recorded to teach about עין הרע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהושע 17:15, read as advice to hide in the forests from the evil eye.
